title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
This is a fabrication and impersonation failure rather than a model error. Photographs of a real, identifiable person were taken from a private account and used to generate explicit images presented as images of her, then circulated under fake accounts on several platforms. The falsehood is not an incidental output of a system, it is the product being distributed, and the fake accounts exist to make the material look like it came from someone other than the person who made it.

The harm sits at the point of use, not at the point of training or deployment. Nothing in the reporting describes a system behaving outside its design, a model asserting something false on its own, or an automated decision made without a human check. What is described is a person operating consumer tools and consumer platforms. Catching it earlier would have required the hosting platforms to detect synthetic intimate imagery or to tie the accounts to a real identity, because the victim learned of the distribution from anonymous messages rather than from any platform notice.

What is not established is which AI tool or service was used, and whether the arrest led to any charge or conviction. The account of resentment comes from an admission during interrogation, which is not a court finding, and the investigation is reported as ongoing.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing sexually explicit AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to create obscene morphed images. He then circulated this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her altered photographs and videos were being shared on Discord servers. She reported the case to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During investigation, police traced digital footprints across the fake profiles and identified Bansal as the perpetrator. He admitted during interrogation that he knew the woman from college and harbored personal resentment toward her. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence, with investigation still ongoing.
